extracted.intended_audience: Users of SINGULAR (computational algebra / algebraic geometry practitioners and developers using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage guidelines for SINGULAR library procedures (gradedModules.lib, hess.lib, methods.lib, modules.lib etc.), including input/output types, assumptions, and examples for constructing graded objects, resolutions, and Riemann–Roch computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: mappingcone usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mappingcone(M,N), M,N graded objects. Return: chain complex (as a list). Purpose: construct a free resolution of the cokernel of a random map between Img(M), and Img(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows LIB "gradedModules.lib"; ring setup; define presentations M and N, compute R=grlifting(M,N), then def T=mappingcone(M,N); the returned chain complex can be inspected with grview(T) which prints graded resolution and maps (d_1 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: mappingcone3 usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: mappingcone3(A,B), graded objects A and B (matrices defining maps). Return: chain complex (as a list). Purpose: construct a free resolution of the cokernel of a random map between M=coker(A) and N=coker(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to call mappingcone3(A,T) and inspect grview(G). Note: the documentation includes comments "// BUG in the proc" for mappingcone3 in multiple examples — users should be aware that mappingcone3 may be buggy or produce unexpected output.

rubrics_metrics.name: grlifting3 (and grlifting family) usage note
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library gradedModules.lib. grlifting3 computes graded liftings between graded presentations (examples: def F=grlifting3(T,A);).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation contains a TODO: "grlifting4 was newer and had more documentation than this proc, but was removed... Please verify and update!" — implies grlifting3 behavior/documentation may be stale; verify interface and prefer newer documented alternatives when available. Example outputs show resulting graded homomorphisms and resolutions (use grview to inspect).

rubrics_metrics.name: grrange input/output contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: grrange(M), graded object M. Return: intvec. Purpose: get weights of module units, thus describing the target of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: module P = grobj(module([xy,0,xz]),intvec(0,1,0)); grrange(P); outputs e.g. 0,1,0. Use grdeg(P) and grview(P) to inspect degrees and graded homomorphism after calling grrange.

rubrics_metrics.name: grneg input/output contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: grneg(A), graded object A. Return: graded object. Purpose: graded map defined by -A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows grview(A) before and after grneg; degrees and graded homomorphism structure are preserved, with entries negated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixpres usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matrixpres(a), intvec a. Return: graded object. Purpose: matrix presentation for direct sum of omega^a[i](i) in form of a graded object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show constructing multiple matrix presentations with different intvec inputs and inspecting via grview; the function constructs graded homomorphisms with particular source/target degrees for later combination into modules/resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: RiemannRochHess assumptions and input formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure RiemannRochHess in hess.lib computes a vector space basis of the Riemann–Roch space L(D) for a divisor D on a function field defined by f. Assumes: all fractional ideals must be represented by a list of size two (first element ideal of k[x,y], second element the common denominator polynomial of k[x]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base ring R must be a ring in two variables x,y or three variables x,y,z. If nvars(R)=2: f must be absolutely irreducible and monic as a polynomial in y. If nvars(R)=3: f must be absolutely irreducible homogeneous polynomial whose dehomogenization w.r.t. z is monic in y. The procedure supports divisorD specified either in 'ideals' representation (list of two ideals) or 'free' representation (list of places with exponents); see below for exact expected structures. Examples given for both nvars=2 and nvars=3 illustrate expected input forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: RiemannRochHess divisor representation: 'ideals' vs 'free'
rubrics_metrics.description: When calling RiemannRochHess(f,divisorD,s): if s='ideals' then divisorD is given in ideal representation; divisorD[1] is the finite ideal (fractional ideal of IntCl(k[x],F)) and divisorD[2] is the infinite ideal. If s='free' then divisorD is a list where each element is [fractional_ideal, exponent] describing finite and infinite places with exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nvars(R)=3 and s='ideals' the two ideals represent the positive and negative part of the divisor respectively (i.e., D = (I) - (J)). Examples show both styles; ensure your input follows the correct shape or the procedure will not interpret D correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: RiemannRochHess output format (RRBasis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: a vector space basis of the Riemann–Roch space of D, stored in a list RRBasis. RRBasis contains a list rbasis and a polynomial den. The basis of L(D) consists of all rational functions g/den where g is an element of rbasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples print multiple entries showing the list elements of the returned basis. Use the returned rbasis and den to form rational functions representing L(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods library: installMethod usage and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: In methods.lib, methods select functions by types of the input tuple. The central function is installMethod, which takes a hashtable associating a tuple of input types to function names and creates the corresponding procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HashTables are lists with arbitrary index sets (created by hashTable); their size can be determined by size; values can be extracted by selectKey or the * operator. HashTables can be combined with addHashTables or +. Methods can be added with the + operator. Use installMethod to dispatch on input type tuples.

rubrics_metrics.name: HashTable operations guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: HashTables: creation and manipulation utilities documented: hashTable to create, size to determine size, selectKey or * to extract values, addHashTables or + to add hash tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HashTables are used to map tuples of input types to function names for creating methods; using the documented operations is necessary to build method dispatch tables correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: modules.lib purpose and type system
rubrics_metrics.description: modules.lib supports computation of graded free resolutions with a custom graduation of monomials. It introduces new classes: Matrix (matrices with source and target free modules), FreeModule (ring and degrees), Resolution (graded resolutions), Module (image, coker, kernel of a matrix or subquotient of two matrices), Ideal (with own base ring saved), Homomorphism (R-module homomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This library is experimental and in-progress. To compute resolutions using modules.lib, matrices should be of the Matrix class (use makeMatrix), and modules may be constructed via image/kernel/coker of these matrices. The library provides specialized procedures (see id, zero, freeModule, makeMatrix, makeIdeal) to construct the necessary objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: id(n) contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: id(n); n integer. Return: returns the n x n identity matrix, with nongraded free modules for source and target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows id(4) printing a 4x4 identity matrix. Use id when a plain identity with non-graded modules is needed; for graded identity or graded modules, construct appropriate freeModule and use makeMatrix if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: zero(n,m) contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: zero(n,m); n and m integer. Return: returns the n x m zero matrix, with nongraded free modules for source and target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows zero(4,3) producing a 4x3 zero matrix. Use zero for ungraded zero matrices; for graded zero matrices, ensure you create appropriately graded FreeModule sources/targets or use makeMatrix to convert.

rubrics_metrics.name: freeModule creation and degree conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: freeModule(r,n,l); r ring, n integer, l list. Return: a free Module over ring r, with rank n, and degrees l for the generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: use -1 for no graduation and 0 to set every degree to 0. Example: freeModule(r,3,list(1,2,3)) prints Degrees of the generators: {1} {2} {3}. Use these conventions when building graded free modules for Matrix sources/targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeMatrix behavior for homogeneous matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeMatrix(m), where m is a standard matrix. RETURN: Matrix, with graded source and target if the matrix is homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: build a plain matrix m[2][2]=x,y3,z,xz; then Matrix M = m; use makeMatrix to convert ordinary matrices into the Matrix class so that graded source/target information is attached automatically when the matrix is homogeneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeIdeal usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeIdeal(i) or Ideal I=i; where i is an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: makeIdeal creates an Ideal object preserving its base ring for use with modules.lib resolution computations. Use makeIdeal before passing ideals into procedures expecting the library's Ideal class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation warnings and examples as authoritative guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Several procedure examples include comments like "// BUG in the proc" and TODO notes (e.g., regarding grlifting4). These are part of the documentation and indicate procedures may have known issues or outdated documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should treat example runs and comments as important guidance: inspect grview outputs, check betti/resolution outputs, and verify results. When encountering unexpected results, consult the comments in the library docs and consider verifying against alternative procedures or updated libraries.
